source_language_policy.notes: All 104 canonical learn-from languages can supply the learner-facing core explanation shell. Source-language support is independent from whether that language is offered as a grammar-learning target.

target_language_policy.notes: The current core lesson implements every Tier 1 and Tier 2 language as a structured grammar target. Tier 3 remains reading/games plus source/comparison support under the product registry.

best_language.description: A language Gef can use as one of the learner's strongest explanation languages for this lesson.
best_language.registry_requirement: The language tag must exist in programs.learnFromLanguages.
best_language.notes: The localized source shell is intentionally independent from target grammar. Do not build 104 × 21 pair-specific lesson files.

learning_language_comparison.description: A language that can participate in the comparison portion without rule-driven practice.
learning_language_comparison.notes: Comparison support describes the language's system without inventing a target grammar path.

learning_language_full.description: A Tier 1/Tier 2 language the lesson can actively teach using structured rules.
learning_language_full.notes: Spanish has safe el/la cloze data. Other languages may have one structured system form so the generic compiler teaches rules without synthesizing bogus two-choice cloze exercises.

trust_visibility.effective_language_trust: Minimum trust state among the assets actually used for that language and role.
trust_visibility.effective_lesson_trust: Minimum trust state among all artifacts rendered in the current lesson session.

full.description: Structured grammatical-gender or no-gender-system rules exist and the language may be selected as a grammar-learning target.

comparison_only.description: The language has explicit source/comparison support but is Tier 3 under the current product policy, so this family does not promise a bespoke grammar lesson path for it.

unavailable.description: No current canonical learn-from language is missing the core source/comparison layer.

promotion_rules: Global language tier never grants lesson-level full support by itself; the current full list is explicit because its structured grammar records now exist.
Tier 3 remains comparison_only under the current product registry even when its comparison record is detailed.
Do not infer a gender inventory from genealogical family, script, article count, or missing data.
A full-support language must be lesson_ready and contain at least one structured form and rule.
Noun-class systems must be represented on their own terms rather than relabeled masculine/feminine/neuter.
A language with no productive grammatical noun gender can still be a full target: the lesson teaches that absence and how the language expresses related meanings instead.
Generated source copy and candidate research remain below human-reviewed trust levels until normal review promotion.
